rmt-2005-gen-01.title: Two equations
rmt-2005-gen-01.body:
Let $x$ be the number of 3-legged goats and $y$ the number of 5-legged goats. Then $x+y=23$ and $3x+5y=83$. Subtracting 3 times the first from the second: $2y=83-69=14$, so $y=7$.

**Answer: 7**

rmt-2005-gen-01.title: Assume all have 3 legs
rmt-2005-gen-01.body:
If all 23 goats had 3 legs there would be 69 legs. The extra $83-69=14$ legs come from 5-legged goats, each contributing 2 extra legs, so there are $14/2=7$ of them.

**Answer: 7**

rmt-2005-gen-02.title: Covering radius of the lattice
rmt-2005-gen-02.body:
Every point of the plane lies in some unit lattice square and is within $\frac{\sqrt2}{2}$ of the nearest corner of it. So a circle of radius greater than $\frac{\sqrt2}2$ always has a lattice point in its interior. The circle centered at $(\frac12,\frac12)$ with radius $\frac{\sqrt2}2$ passes through four lattice points but contains none in its interior. The maximum area is $\pi\left(\frac{\sqrt2}2\right)^2=\frac\pi2$.

**Answer: $\frac\pi2$**

rmt-2005-gen-03.title: Compare lengths
rmt-2005-gen-03.body:
Let the city radius be $r$ and the angle between the roads $\theta$. Walking along the two roads via the center is $r+r=2r$. Walking along the wall is the arc $r\theta$. Setting $2r=r\theta$ gives $\theta=2$ radians.

**Answer: 2 radians**

rmt-2005-gen-04.title: Complementary counting
rmt-2005-gen-04.body:
Total 4-digit strings from $\{1,2,3\}$: $3^4=81$. Those with no 1: $2^4=16$; no 2: $16$; neither 1 nor 2 (all 3s): $1$. Containing both $=81-16-16+1=50$.

**Answer: 50**

rmt-2005-gen-05.title: Frobenius number
rmt-2005-gen-05.body:
For coprime $m,n$ the largest non-representable integer is $mn-m-n$. Here $13\cdot7-13-7=71$.

**Answer: 71**

rmt-2005-gen-06.title: Count days
rmt-2005-gen-06.body:
February 26, 2005 was a Saturday (the date of this tournament). From February 26 to December 8, 2005 is $285$ days; $285=7\cdot40+5$, so December 8, 2005 was a Saturday $+5$ = Thursday. From December 8, 2005 to December 8, 2019 there are $14$ years $=14\cdot365$ days (a multiple of 7) plus 3 leap days (2008, 2012, 2016), so the weekday advances by 3: Thursday $+3$ = Sunday.

**Answer: Sunday**

rmt-2005-gen-07.title: Count outcomes
rmt-2005-gen-07.body:
Fix the 4-sided die value $k\in\{1,2,3,4\}$. The two 20-sided dice must sum to $21-k$, which can be done in $20-k$ ways ($19,18,17,16$ for $k=1,\dots,4$), total $70$ favorable outcomes out of $20\cdot20\cdot4=1600$. Probability $=\frac{70}{1600}=\frac7{160}$.

**Answer: $\frac7{160}$**

rmt-2005-gen-08.title: Powers of 26
rmt-2005-gen-08.body:
The number of trailing zeros in base 26 is the largest $k$ with $26^k\mid2005!$. Since $26=2\cdot13$ and 2 is far more plentiful than 13 in $2005!$, count factors of 13: $\lfloor2005/13\rfloor+\lfloor2005/169\rfloor=154+11=165$ ($13^3=2197>2005$).

**Answer: 165**

rmt-2005-gen-10.title: Parallelograms inscribed in a circle are rectangles
rmt-2005-gen-10.body:
The lattice points with $x^2+y^2=50$ are $(\pm1,\pm7),(\pm7,\pm1),(\pm5,\pm5)$: 12 points on a circle. A parallelogram inscribed in a circle is a rectangle, whose diagonals are diameters. The 12 points form 6 antipodal pairs, and any 2 of the 6 diameters determine one rectangle, so there are $\binom62=15$.

**Answer: 15**

rmt-2005-gen-11.title: Permutations with repeated words
rmt-2005-gen-11.body:
The problem sentence has 18 words: in, how, many, different, ways, can, the, words, in, this, problem, be, ordered, including, the, words, in, parentheses. The word \"in\" appears 3 times, \"the\" twice and \"words\" twice. The number of distinct orderings is $\frac{18!}{3!\,2!\,2!}=\frac{18!}{24}=266{,}765{,}571{,}072{,}000$.

**Answer: $\frac{18!}{24}$**

rmt-2005-gen-12.title: Sectors around the pen
rmt-2005-gen-12.body:
From the corner, the dog sweeps a $270^\circ$ sector of radius 30: area $\frac34\cdot\pi\cdot30^2=675\pi$. Going around the corner at the end of the 10 ft side, 20 ft of leash remain: a quarter circle of radius 20, area $100\pi$. Going around the corner at the end of the 20 ft side, 10 ft of leash remain: a quarter circle of radius 10, area $25\pi$. Going around any further corner would need more than the remaining leash, and these three regions do not overlap. Total $675\pi+100\pi+25\pi=800\pi$.

**Answer: $800\pi$ square feet**

rmt-2005-gen-13.title: Powers of 2 among four consecutive integers
rmt-2005-gen-13.body:
Among $n,n+1,n+2,n+3$ two are even: one is $\equiv2\pmod4$ (contributing exactly one factor of 2) and the other is a multiple of 4. We need $2^7$ in total, so the multiple of 4 must contribute $2^6$, i.e. be a multiple of 64. The smallest such block starting from the left is $61,62,63,64$ (the multiple of 64 is the last term, $64\cdot62\cdot63\cdot61$ has $2^6\cdot2=2^7$). No block starting below 61 contains 64 or any multiple of 64.

**Answer: 61**

rmt-2005-gen-14.title: Similar triangles and a geometric series
rmt-2005-gen-14.body:
The right triangles $AEB$ (right angle at $B$) and $EBD$ (right angle at $D$) are similar, so $\frac{EB}{AE}=\frac{ED}{EB}$, giving $EB^2=16\cdot8=128$ and $EB=8\sqrt2$. Then $BD=\sqrt{EB^2-ED^2}=8$. Each successive triangle is similar to the previous with ratio $\frac{EB}{AE}=\frac{\sqrt2}2$, so the vertical segments $16,8,4,\dots$ form a geometric series with ratio $\left(\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right)^2=\frac12$. Sum $=\frac{16}{1-\frac12}=32$.

**Answer: 32**

rmt-2005-gen-15.title: Residues mod 5
rmt-2005-gen-15.body:
Count the pairs by residues mod 5. The 12-sided die has residue 0 twice (5, 10), residue 1 three times (1, 6, 11), residue 2 three times (2, 7, 12), residue 3 twice (3, 8) and residue 4 twice (4, 9). The 8-sided die has residue 0 once (5), residue 1 twice (1, 6), residue 2 twice (2, 7), residue 3 twice (3, 8) and residue 4 once (4). Pairs with sum $\equiv0$: $(0,0):2\cdot1=2$; $(1,4):3\cdot1=3$; $(2,3):3\cdot2=6$; $(3,2):2\cdot2=4$; $(4,1):2\cdot2=4$. Total $19$ of $96$.

**Answer: $\frac{19}{96}$**

rmt-2005-gen-16.title: Replace x by -x
rmt-2005-gen-16.body:
The power $x^{1000}$ is even, so its coefficient is unchanged by $x\to-x$. This turns $(1-x^2+x^5)^{2005}$ into $(1-x^2-x^5)^{2005}$ and $(1+x^2-x^5)^{2005}$ into $(1+x^2+x^5)^{2005}$.

In $(1+x^2+x^5)^{2005}$ every term has a positive coefficient, while in $(1-x^2-x^5)^{2005}$ each term is $\pm$ the corresponding term of the first expansion, a term using $b$ factors $x^2$ and $c$ factors $x^5$ (with $2b+5c=1000$) has sign $(-1)^{b+c}$. Such terms with $b+c$ odd exist, e.g. $b=495,c=2$, so some contributions to the coefficient are negative, while all contributions to the other coefficient are positive and the two sets of terms are otherwise identical in size. So the coefficient from $(1+x^2-x^5)^{2005}$ is strictly larger.

**Answer: the coefficient in $(1+x^2-x^5)^{2005}$ is bigger**

rmt-2005-gen-17.title: Choose positions of the 7s, then order the rest
rmt-2005-gen-17.body:
A block can be placed only after the block under it. The blocks 1, 3, 5 sit on 2, 4, 6 respectively, and the three 7s form a column. The three 7s are indistinguishable, so only their positions in the sequence matter: $\binom93=84$ choices (they are then forced to be stacked bottom to top).

The six remaining positions are filled with $1,\dots,6$ in an order where $2$ precedes $1$, $4$ precedes $3$ and $6$ precedes $5$. Each of the three constraints halves the count, giving $\frac{6!}{2^3}=90$.

Total $84\cdot90=7560$.

**Answer: 7560**

rmt-2005-gen-18.title: Count the powers
rmt-2005-gen-18.body:
Powers of 4 up to $10^6$: $4^0,\dots,4^9$ ($4^9=262144$, $4^{10}>10^6$): 10 numbers. Powers of 6: $6^0,\dots,6^7$ ($6^7=279936$, $6^8>10^6$): 8 numbers. A number that is both a power of 4 and of 6 must be $1$ (since $4^a=6^b$ forces $a=b=0$), so only $1$ is counted twice. Total $10+8-1=17$ (counting $1=4^0=6^0$ as a power).

**Answer: 17**

rmt-2005-gen-19.title: Time until the walls meet
rmt-2005-gen-19.body:
The walls approach each other at $20+20=40$ ft/s, so they meet after $\frac{100}{40}=2.5$ s. The ball moves at a constant 25 ft/s the whole time, so it travels $25\cdot2.5=62.5$ ft.

**Answer: 62.5 ft**

rmt-2005-gen-20.title: When is n^n a cube
rmt-2005-gen-20.body:
If $3\mid n$, then $n^n=\left(n^{n/3}\right)^3$ is a cube: $33$ values ($3,6,\dots,99$). Otherwise write $n=a^b$ with $a$ not a perfect power; then $n^n=a^{bn}$ is a cube iff $3\mid bn$. If $3\nmid n$ this means $3\mid b$, i.e. $n$ is a perfect cube: $1,8,27,64$ in range, of which $1,8,64$ are not multiples of 3. Total $33+3=36$.

**Answer: 36**

rmt-2005-gen-21.title: Need gcd 1
rmt-2005-gen-21.body:
A subset can measure 1 mL exactly when the gcd of its sizes is 1. The sizes factor as $30=2\cdot3\cdot5$, $42=2\cdot3\cdot7$, $70=2\cdot5\cdot7$, $105=3\cdot5\cdot7$, $210=2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot7$. Any three of the first four share a prime factor (each prime misses exactly one container among them), and adding 210 changes nothing. So at least four containers are needed, and among four containers $\{30,42,70,105\}$ is the only choice with gcd 1 that avoids 210 (any set containing 210 together with three others has a common prime factor). Its sum is $30+42+70+105=247$.

**Answer: 247**

rmt-2005-gen-22.title: Case analysis
rmt-2005-gen-22.body:
If $x,y$ have the same sign, $|x+y|=|x|+|y|$ and the equation is $|x|+|y|=\frac12$: the lines $x+y=\pm\frac12$ in the first and third quadrants. If they have opposite signs, $|x+y|+|x|+|y|=2\max(|x|,|y|)$, so $\max(|x|,|y|)=\frac12$: the segments $x=\pm\frac12$ and $y=\pm\frac12$ in the second and fourth quadrants. The curve is a hexagon with vertices $(\frac12,0),(0,\frac12),(-\frac12,\frac12),(-\frac12,0),(0,-\frac12),(\frac12,-\frac12)$. It consists of two squares of side $\frac12$ and two right isosceles triangles with legs $\frac12$: area $2\cdot\frac14+2\cdot\frac18=\frac34$.

**Answer: $\frac34$**

rmt-2005-gen-24.title: Separate the pattern from the letters
rmt-2005-gen-24.body:
MATHEMATICS has 4 vowels (A, E, A, I) and 7 consonants (M, T, H, M, T, C, S). First choose which positions are vowels (the pattern), then arrange the letters.

The 4 vowels split the consonants into 5 blocks (before, between, after), with sizes summing to 7. No block may exceed 2 (no three consonants in a row), and the first and last blocks are at most 1 (not beginning/ending with two consonants). The maximum total is $1+2+2+2+1=8$, so exactly one block is one short: 5 patterns.

Arrangements: vowels $\frac{4!}{2!}=12$; consonants $\frac{7!}{2!\,2!}=1260$. Total $5\cdot12\cdot1260=75600=15\cdot7!$.

**Answer: 75600**

rmt-2005-gen-25.title: Linearity of expectation
rmt-2005-gen-25.body:
There are 32 adjacent pairs of positions in a string of 33 bits, and each pair is \"00\" with probability $\frac14$. By linearity of expectation the expected count is $32\cdot\frac14=8$.

**Answer: 8**
